title: Avoiding Reverse Fall in Drainage Installations
description: One of the most common and damaging installation mistakes in residential drainage is creating a reverse fall, also known as negative slope. When horizontal drainage pipes are installed without the proper downward gradient toward the main sewer or septic line, wastewater cannot flow freely. Solids settle at the low points, leading to recurring clogs, slow drainage, and potential pipe failure over time. Professional plumbers always verify alignment using accurate measuring tools rather than relying on visual estimation alone. Ensuring a consistent downward slope is essential for protecting the entire sanitary system.
